hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) can significantly enhance drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction by leveraging their ability to process and integrate vast amounts of sequence and structural data, potentially improving the prediction of binding affinities beyond traditional methods. The use of deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has already shown promise in modeling protein sequences and drug compounds for DTI predictions, achieving superior performance in binding affinity prediction tasks [deepdta:0][deepdta:1]. By incorporating LLMs, which excel in understanding complex patterns and relationships in large datasets, the accuracy and efficiency of DTI predictions could be further improved, offering a robust tool for drug discovery and development [deepdta:6].
